module_summary: Sequential 16x16 multiplier using shift-and-add with 3-state FSM controlling HOLD, SPIN (compute), and FIN (done) phases.

anchors.name: s
anchors.why: Start command: when asserted with HOLD state, initiates multiplication by loading operands.

anchors.name: a
anchors.why: Input operand A (16-bit); loaded into multiplicand register on start.

anchors.name: b
anchors.why: Input operand B (16-bit); loaded into multiplier register on start.

anchors.name: p
anchors.why: Output product (32-bit result); driven by accumulator register.

anchors.name: bz
anchors.why: Busy flag output: high when FSM state is SPIN (computing).

anchors.name: d
anchors.why: Done flag output: high when FSM state is FIN (multiplication complete).

anchors.name: st
anchors.why: 3-state FSM register: HOLD (idle), SPIN (computing), FIN (done) controlling multiplication sequence.

anchors.name: sum
anchors.why: Accumulator register for partial products in shift-and-add algorithm.

anchors.name: ctr
anchors.why: 5-bit cycle counter; counts down from 0 to detect completion of 16 iterations.

anchors.name: load
anchors.why: Load control flag: gates operand loading into multiplicand and multiplier registers.

anchors.name: mplier
anchors.why: Multiplier shift register: holds and right-shifts operand B during SPIN phase.

anchors.name: mcand
anchors.why: Multiplicand shift register: holds and left-shifts operand A during SPIN phase.

groups.name: Control FSM
groups.description: 3-state FSM managing multiplication phases: HOLD/SPIN/FIN with transitions based on start and completion.

groups.name: Data accumulation
groups.description: Accumulator and partial product computation for shift-and-add algorithm.

groups.name: Operand pipeline
groups.description: Shift registers holding and shifting operands during multiplication iterations.

groups.name: Iteration control
groups.description: Counter and cycle-completion detection for 16-bit multiplication.

groups.name: Input/output interface
groups.description: Start command, operand inputs, product output, and status signals (busy, done).
